The bell above the door gave a thin, cracked jingle as Leo stepped inside. Dust hung in the air like tiny floating stars, and the shelves leaned towards each other as if sharing secrets.

Behind the counter sat Mrs Okafor, who had run the shop for forty years. She did not look up. "We close in ten minutes," she said, turning a page.

Leo hesitated. He had walked past the shop every day for a year and never once gone in. Now, clutching the crumpled note from his grandfather, he took a deep breath and walked to the counter.
